newsitem.title: CHINA: Thailand waives visas for new HK passport.
newsitem.headline: Thailand waives visas for new HK passport.

text.p: Thailand on Wednesday joined a growing list of nations recognising the new passport issued by Hong Kong's post-colonial government.
Speaking after signing a mutual visa exemption pact with Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasan, Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa said he was sure other countries would follow.
"The signing of the agreement reflects the Thai Government's confidence in the "one country, two systems" concept and Hong Kong's continued stability and prosperity," Tung said.
A total of 35 countries including Britain, the United States, Japan and Singapore, have granted visa-free treatment to the new passport which Hong Kong starts issuing this month.

A further five nations are giving the passport the same treatment as the British National Overseas (BNO) passport, which the British government issued to Hong Kong people as a travel document without right of abode in Britain.

About 80 countries allow visa-free entry to BNO passports, which will remain valid travel documents even though Hong Kong formally passed under Chinese sovereignty on Monday night ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Indonesian officials, apparently fearing an influx, sprang a surprise on Tuesday by abruptly cancelling visa-free access for BNO passports immediately after Hong Kong became part of China.

But immigration authorities later said BNO passport-holders did not need visas to enter Indonesia. "They can enter Indonesia without visas," immigration spokesman Mursanuddin Ghani told Reuters in Dkarta by telephone.
The official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday that a number of BNO passport holders were blocked from boarding a Cathay Pacific flight to Indonesia on July 1 and were told they needed visas.
The agency, reporting from Hong Kong, said the rejection was ordered following advice from the Directorate of Immigration in Jakarta.

Ghani said the immigration office was aware of the rejection and reiterated that BNO holders could enter Indonesia without visa. He did not say why the group was blocked on Tuesday and gave no further details.
